# Flox Environments

Curated by Skill Harbor: a guide to creating reproducible development environments with Flox, a declarative environment manager built on Nix with access to over 150,000 packages. One TOML manifest defines the whole toolchain, and every developer on the team gets identical packages, tools, and configuration across macOS and Linux, without containers or VMs. The skill covers the cases where Flox earns its keep: system-level packages (compilers, databases, native libraries) alongside language dependencies, exact version pinning for a whole team, onboarding new developers onto a working setup in minutes, running local services like PostgreSQL, Redis, or Kafka, and killing "works on my machine" for good, including agent and vibe-coding setups that need project-scoped tools without sudo. By @affaan-m, listed here with credit to its creator. From the affaan-m/ECC repository (MIT). Honest caveats: the Flox CLI must be installed (free and open source); macOS and Linux only, no Windows support. Skill Harbor never reviews the code, review it yourself before use.
